claims.title: onFailure event payload shape assumed without validation
claims.text:
🔴 **High**

**onFailure event payload shape assumed without validation**

The onFailure handler casts `event` to `{ data: { event: ListingConditionConfirmedEvent } }` and accesses `event.data.event.data.listingId` without any runtime check. If Inngest's onFailure payload shape differs slightly (e.g., across SDK versions) or `event.data.event` is undefined, this throws inside the failure handler itself, silently swallowing the intended recovery (agent_blocked=true, status revert) and leaving the listing stuck in an inconsistent state (condition_confirmed=true, status=condition_gate, no visible failure indication). Add a defensive check before dereferencing nested properties.

claims.title: `event.data.event.data.listingId` is derived via a double `unknown` cast (`event as unknown as { data: { event: ListingConditionConfirmedEvent } }`). This relies on undocumented internal shape of the `onFailure` callback's `event` parameter (which per Inngest's API typically wraps the original event under `event.data.event`). If this shape is wrong or changes, `listingId` will silently be `undefined`, `if (!listingId) return` will fire, and the failure recovery (agent_blocked=true, status revert) will silently never execute — meaning a listing could get permanently stuck in `condition_confirmed=true`/`condition_gate` with no automated recovery and no error surfaced. Given this is the sole safety net for exhausted retries, consider verifying this shape against the installed Inngest SDK types rather than double-casting through `unknown`, or add a guard/log when the shape doesn't match expectations.

claims.title: Duplicate/concurrent condition-reassessment runs could double-fire the gate transition
claims.text:
🟢 **Low**

**Duplicate/concurrent condition-reassessment runs could double-fire the gate transition**

This two-step update (write condition fields, then separately flip status via a second `.update()` gated on `status='in_loop'`) is not atomic with the first update. If `condition-reassessment` runs twice concurrently for the same listing (e.g. duplicate event delivery), both instances could pass the `.eq('status','in_loop')` guard on the second update if timed right after the first one's condition write but before its status write — actually the status guard does protect against double status flips since only one will match 'in_loop'. However, there is no re-read/lock between the two update calls, so if the user is already mid-condition_gate flow when a second condition-reassessment fires, this second update is silently skipped (fine) — but if it fires before the first transition lands, both compete on `.eq('status','in_loop')` and one will fail silently with no error being surfaced (the result isn't checked). This is a minor correctness gap but likely benign given single-writer semantics elsewhere in the codebase.

This isn't a crash, but it is a silent data-loss path on the documented failure/retry flow.

claims.text:

**Compensation revert re-opens the gate without re-checking Inngest failure was really transient**

When `inngest.send` throws, the code reverts `condition_confirmed` back to its prior value but does not revert `status` (comment says status was never changed, which is correct) — however it also does not restore the CAS: after the revert, `status` is still `condition_gate` and `condition_confirmed` is back to `existing.condition_confirmed`, but the row was already updated in the primary CAS update, meaning a concurrent second request that read `existing` before the first request's update (both requests could pass the `.select` step conceptually) is not actually possible here since the CAS update itself is atomic — this is fine. No actionable issue beyond the extra_notes loss noted separately.

claims.title: onFailure unconditionally clears condition_confirmed/status even if listing already advanced past condition_gate
claims.text:
🟡 **Medium**

**onFailure unconditionally clears condition_confirmed/status even if listing already advanced past condition_gate**

The `onFailure` handler updates `status='condition_gate'` and `condition_confirmed=false` without any CAS/status guard, unlike the CAS-guarded update in `transition-to-in-loop`. If the rewrite actually succeeded (title/description/platform_fields written) but the final `transition-to-in-loop` step failed for an unrelated transient reason before `onFailure` fires (e.g. exhausted retries hit only after the second step failed repeatedly), this would revert a listing that has correct rewritten copy back into condition_gate and mark it `condition_confirmed=false`, forcing the user to redo the review even though the rewrite already completed. Consider adding `.eq('status', 'condition_gate')` here too, or checking whether `condition_confirmed` is still true before reverting, to avoid clobbering a listing that's mid-transition.

claims.title: Silent no-op when zero rows updated on final status transition
claims.text:
🟡 **Medium**

**Silent no-op when zero rows updated on final status transition**

When `updated` is null (zero rows matched, e.g. listing was archived or the status changed concurrently), this only logs a `console.warn` and the function still returns `{ ok: true, listingId }`. The rewrite completed and copy was persisted, but the status transition to `in_loop` silently failed to apply — if this happens because of a transient race rather than an intentional archive, the listing is stuck in `condition_gate` with `condition_confirmed: true` and the UI will show "Rewriting copy…" indefinitely with no automatic retry, since the Inngest run itself reports success.

claims.title: platform_fields rewrite is silently skipped for platforms whose entry doesn't already exist in the DB
claims.text:
🟡 **Medium**

**platform_fields rewrite is silently skipped for platforms whose entry doesn't already exist in the DB**

`updatedPlatformFields.ebay` / `.poshmark` are only patched when `existingPf.ebay` / `existingPf.poshmark` already exist (truthy). If a listing has not yet had platform_fields populated for a platform (e.g. `poshmark` hasn't been generated yet, or the key is absent/null for any reason), the rewritten `poshmark_title`/`poshmark_description` from the Claude call are silently discarded — no error, no log, and the returned data implies success. Since the PR description states 'titles + descriptions + condition_notes updated' as a guaranteed outcome of this flow, this is a correctness gap: the rewrite can complete successfully while leaving stale/missing copy for a platform that lacks a pre-existing platform_fields entry, and there's no test or log signaling this happened.

claims.title: extra_notes/observations validated but not persisted on the listing

**extra_notes/observations validated but not persisted on the listing**

`extra_notes` is validated (type + length) and forwarded to Inngest as `extraNotes`, where it's used transiently in the rewrite prompt (`rewrite-listing.ts`), but it is never written back to the `listings` row anywhere in this diff. If the rewrite fails and the user needs to retry, or if anyone later wants to inspect what observations were submitted, that data is lost — it only exists for the duration of a single Inngest run's prompt construction. This may be intentional, but it's worth confirming this isn't meant to be persisted (e.g., appended to `condition_notes` or stored in a dedicated column) since the UI collects it as user-authored content.

replies.author: joeblackwaslike
replies.body: The path is correct. Inngest `onFailure` handlers receive a synthetic `inngest/function.failed` event whose `data` object wraps the original triggering event at `data.event`. So `event.data.event.data.listingId` is the right access path for the original `listing/condition-confirmed` event's listingId. The `as unknown as` cast is the standard TypeScript pattern for Inngest failure events (the SDK doesn't export a typed failure envelope).
